messages:
leo: kicking off phased rollout for driver 540 + CUDA 12.2 + NCCL 2.18 to Dedicated fleet (us-west-2). Canary set: dedicated-canary-3 (4 nodes). Plan: 4 -> 40% -> 75% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. starting 12:30 PT. any red flags?

maya: heads-up — our multi-GPU batch tests flaked in staging with NCCL timeouts after a similar lib bump. worth watching closely. :eyes:

simon: saw this on canary-1 just now: `NCCL WARN allreduce failed with timeout` followed by `gpu: rm 0 fatal error` in dmesg. single job but reproducible on rank=0. uploading logs.

anya: i'm oncall — paused the next phase. collecting core and nv-peer memory stats. saving to s3://redwood-artifacts/nccl/1742501234.tar.gz

deploy-bot: Deployment started for canary group dedicated-canary-3 -> driver:540 cuda:12.2 nccl:2.18 (request id: dpl-9802).

julian: thanks. if this is kernel/driver incompat we should rollback driver on canary and pin CUDA lib versions for the rollout. can we do a fast rollback?

leo: yes we have rollback play: `fleetctl apply --rollback --group dedicated-canary-3 --driver 535` — low-risk. but need to confirm stateful jobs cleaned up.

maya: reproducer attached: short script that runs nccl allreduce across 4 GPUs (torch.distributed) — reproduces ~80% within 10m on canary-1. posting snippet.

maya: ```bash
# repro
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=4 nccl_repro.py --iters 200
```

simon: stack trace from kernel ring buffer: `nv_peer_mem: page fault on addr` and `gpucrash: TLB shootdown` — looks like driver/ABI mismatch with our pinned kernel module.

anya: i'm dumping module versions now: `nvidia.ko` shows version 535.112, package shows 540.2 in the image — mismatch. that explains the crash.

leo: big flag: some of our images were built with the new driver bits but the node kernel module wasn't updated due to a packaging race. need atomic driver swap in the image build or we risk mixed states.

ops-bot: Alert: canary health droppped below 90% for multi-gpu jobs in us-west-2. Auto-pause enabled.

julian: action items: 1) rollback canary -> driver 535 (leo) 2) stop rollout phases (leo/maya) 3) audit image builder to ensure kernel module & package align (infra) 4) add gating test for mixed-module detection (sre)

leo: i'm executing rollback now. running: ```bash
fleetctl ssh --group dedicated-canary-3 -- "sudo systemctl stop rdedu && sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-535 --yes && sudo reboot"
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued (job id rb-44). attempting drain of user jobs with 10m grace.

maya: monitoring memory and NCCL errors — at t+6m after rollback start errors dropped to baseline on 3/4 nodes. one node still showing dmesg gpu errors, digging in.

simon: that node had the mixed 540 kernel module. kernel logs show the module didn't replace because apt transaction failed (lock conflict). created PR to add post-install checks to our image builder.

anya: created incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian/incidents/INC-2026-driver-rollout (details + artifacts). paging customer success for impacted Dedicated customers.

leo: postmortem plan: 1) add preflight check in rollout operator to ensure node module == package version 2) add canary gate: run a short multi-gpu NCCL allreduce before expanding 3) extend canary hold windows to 45m for driver upgrades 4) automate rollback faster via `fleetctl rollback` path 5) cost note: rollback cost ~2.1 GPU-hours but avoided larger impact.

julian: agree. also we should add a metric for `module_version_mismatch` and alert if >0 in a pool.

ops-bot: Rollback succeeded on 3/4 nodes, node-3 scheduled for manual repro image reprovision.

maya: closing loop with model infra team — they will pin CUDA toolkit in images and add packaging check. i'll follow up with PR.

leo: thanks everyone. we'll reschedule a safer phased rollout next week after fixes. :thumbsup:
